name: Trojan Library
subtitle: an archive that orbits with Earth, fuel-free

effects.effect: a small body stays put relative to two big orbiting bodies at balance points

effect: a small body stays put relative to two big orbiting bodies at balance points
how: Libraries on Earth burn, flood and are forgotten, and a store on the Moon sits in dust under constant bombardment. Glass discs etched with humanity's records are parked 60 degrees ahead of Earth along its orbit, a balance point between Sun and Earth (Lagrangian point) where an object stays put for thousands of years without fuel, beyond wars and weather and findable by anyone who knows where to look.
obstacle: Reading it means flying a probe 150 million km, so it is a backup for catastrophe, not a library to visit.
why: A civilisation backup that needs no upkeep, no power and no planet.
real: The Arch Mission Foundation has announced plans for Arch Libraries at Sun-Earth L4/L5 (target 2027); its existing archive is in heliocentric orbit, and no L4/L5 archive has flown.
